lines.japanese: えーと、まー、どーでもいいことなんですけどー。
lines.english: Well, uh, this doesn't really matter, but...

lines.japanese: ダイヤル式の電話ってあるじゃないですか。ジーコ、ジーコっていう。
lines.english: You know rotary phones? The ones that went *whirr-click, whirr-click*.

lines.japanese: アレって今では割とレアアイテムになってますけど、実はその前の世代からすると画期的な発明だったんですよね。
lines.english: They're something of a rarity now, but to the generation that came before, the rotary dial was a revolutionary invention.

lines.japanese: それがいつしか留守番電話や子機の普及に伴い、そして近年に至って携帯電話の登場によって、急速に姿を消していったわけです。
lines.english: Then answering machines and cordless phones became commonplace. More recently, cell phones arrived, and rotary phones rapidly disappeared.

lines.japanese: そうして、最近では公衆電話なんてものもとんと姿を見かけなくなってきました。昔はそれこそ個人商店だとか駅だとか、人の集まる場所には必ずあったんですけどね。
lines.english: These days, even public phones have all but disappeared. Once, you found one at every little shop, every station—anywhere people gathered.

lines.japanese: 真っ暗な夜道を歩いていると、公衆電話の明かりがほっと安心させてくれたり、ドラマの緊迫したシーンに使われたり、まだまだ需要はあると思うんですけどね。
lines.english: On a pitch-black road at night, the light from a public phone could set your mind at ease. They were fixtures in tense scenes on TV, too. I still think they have their uses.

lines.japanese: これからも有形文化財として、その形だけでも残して欲しいものです。
lines.english: At the very least, I hope we preserve their form as part of our tangible cultural heritage.

lines.japanese: いやあ、電話って本当にいいものですね。
lines.english: And there you have it, folks: telephones truly are wonderful things.

lines.japanese: 「来るなり何を延々語りだしたかと思えば……おまえもそろそろ携帯電話の一つでも持ったらどうだ」
lines.english: “I wondered what could have possessed you to launch into this endless speech the moment you arrived... Buy yourself a cell phone already.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、機会があれば。ただ今回は事務室の電話をお借りできないかと思いまして」
lines.english: “Yes, when the opportunity arises. For now, I was hoping to borrow the office phone.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅーむ……いや、実は言いにくいことだから黙っていたのだが……」
lines.english: “Hmmm... The truth is, I kept silent because this is difficult to say...”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんすか。そんな、まるで軽部狩男を見るときの女子スタッフみたいな顔しちゃって」
lines.english: “Wh-what is it? You've got the exact same look the women on staff get whenever they see Karuo Karube.”

lines.japanese: 「なにっ？　おかしいな、苦虫を噛み潰したような表情を作ったはずだが」
lines.english: “What? How strange. I meant to look as though I'd just swallowed something unspeakably bitter.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、そのまんまですよね」
lines.english: “Yes. That's exactly it.”

lines.japanese: 「だがこの苦渋はおまえのせいなのだ。先月合コンを催したときに事務室の電話を貸しただろう」
lines.english: “But you are the cause of this bitterness. I lent you the office phone when you held that group date last month, did I not?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、紀奈子さんの壮行会のときにお借りしましたね」
lines.english: “Yes. I borrowed it for Kinako's farewell party.”

lines.japanese: 「うむ、その合コンを行った月なんだが、電話代の請求書が普段の倍近い金額で送りつけられてきたのだ」
lines.english: “Indeed. But the phone bill for that month came in at almost twice the usual amount.”

lines.japanese: 「さてはお前、神聖なる事務所でいかがわしい番号をダイヤルしただろう。そうでなければ、あの値段は納得できん」
lines.english: “You must have dialed some indecent number from the sacred office. Nothing else could explain the bill.”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、本気でおっしゃってるなら続きは法廷で」
lines.english: “Uh, if this is a serious accusation, you can make the rest of your case in court.”

lines.japanese: 「フフ、だが本当はおまえもかけたんだろ？　なあ、男同士で秘密を共有しようぜ」
lines.english: “Heh heh. But you really did call one, didn't you? Come now. Let us share our secret as men.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、すいません、そういう男子中学生みたいな馴れ合いとか今度にしてください。とにかくいまは事務室の電話を貸して欲しいんですお願いします」
lines.english: “Sorry, but can we save the middle-school-boy bonding for another time? I need the office phone now. Please.”

lines.japanese: 「ならばおまえも、出来心でついうっかりピンクなダイヤルにアクセスしてしまったと自供しろ。さもなければ電話は貸せん」
lines.english: “Then confess that, in one weak and careless moment, you called a premium adult line. Otherwise, the phone is forbidden to you.”

lines.japanese: 「ああもう、分かりました分かりました。ふん、仕方ありませんね、今日はわりかし真剣モードなんで、少しばかり手荒にいきやしょう」
lines.english: “Fine, fine, I get it. Hmph. You've left me no choice. I'm in serious mode today, so I'm afraid we'll have to do this the hard way.”

lines.japanese: 俺は太極拳よろしく適当な呼吸法をしながら、円を描くように両手を回しました。
lines.english: I began circling both hands through the air, breathing however I imagined one did in tai chi.

lines.japanese: 「なに、この俺に戦いを挑むだと？　ほほう、牙は抜けたといえど、爪まで錆びつかせた覚えはないぞ。いいだろう、かかってこい鷲介！　おまえが俺を超えるにはまだ早い！」
lines.english: “What? You dare challenge me? Ho! My fangs may be gone, but my claws have not yet rusted. Very well—come at me, Shusuke! You are not yet ready to surpass me!”

lines.japanese: 「この狩男、伊達に３５年間を生きてきたわけではないぞ！　思春期の多感な年頃に河原で出会った成人向け雑誌がかなりにハードコアなＳＭものだったためトラウマとなってこの技を生みだした！　ゆくぞ！」
lines.english: “This Karuo has not lived thirty-five years in vain! In the tender bloom of adolescence, I found an adult magazine on a riverbank—such hardcore S&M that the trauma gave birth to this technique! Now, behold!”

lines.japanese: <10>\「コール・ミー・クィィィィ──ン！！」
lines.english: <10> “CALL! ME! QUEEEEEEN!!”

lines.japanese: <10>\「うぜええええ――っ！」
lines.english: <10> “YOU'RE SO GODDAMN ANNOYING!!”

lines.japanese: 「おっさん！　恥ずかしい遊びは控え室でやれって言ってんだろ！　客どころか外の通行人まで、店ん中ガン見してんじゃねえか！」
lines.english: “Old man! I told you to keep your humiliating games in the staff room! Forget the customers—even people outside are stopping to stare into the restaurant!”

lines.japanese: 「ああ英里子さん、丁度よかった。面白い話があるんすよ、実はきのう、マスターのビデオラックに鍵がかかってなくて扉がたまたま開いてたんすけどね」
lines.english: “Ah, Eriko, perfect timing. I have a funny story. Yesterday, you see, the boss's video cabinet happened to be unlocked, and the door just happened to be open—”

lines.japanese: 「鷲介ェェェ！　よし、行け！　今すぐ事務室へ突っ走って、思うさま電話をかけまくれ！　なんならセットでパソコンをいじり倒しても構わん！　興奮がおさまるまでしっぽり楽しむがいい！」
lines.english: “Shusukeeee! Fine, go! Race to the office this instant and make all the calls your heart desires! I'll even throw in the computer—use it as hard as you like! Enjoy yourself until every last ounce of excitement is spent!”

lines.japanese: 「すいません、恩に着ます！」
lines.english: “Thank you. I owe you one!”

lines.japanese: 俺が店内の階段を上っていくと、入れ替わりに外の非常階段を下る音が聞こえてきました。
lines.english: As I climbed the stairs inside, I heard someone descending the outdoor fire escape in the opposite direction.

lines.japanese: ああ、もしかして日和子さんはこれから仕事に入るのかなあ……。
lines.english: Ah. Maybe Hiyoko was about to start her shift...

lines.japanese: 先に挨拶しておこうかとも思いましたが、説明がいろいろと大変そうなので、俺はまっすぐ事務室へ向かいました。
lines.english: I considered saying hello first, but there would have been too much to explain, so I went straight to the office.

lines.japanese: スタッフルームにはさいわい誰もいませんでした。
lines.english: Fortunately, the staff room was empty.

lines.japanese: 俺は受話器を持ちあげると、記憶を呼びおこして米田さんの番号をプッシュします。
lines.english: I picked up the receiver, dredged Yoneda's number from memory, and pressed the buttons.

lines.japanese: うーん……出ないなあ……。
lines.english: Hmm... No answer...

lines.japanese: 職業柄なのか米田さんは、出られない状況ならマナーモードにするひとなんだけど、保留メッセージが流れるわけでもなし……。
lines.english: Maybe it came with the job, but Yoneda put her phone on silent whenever she couldn't answer. Yet there wasn't even a voicemail greeting...

lines.japanese: 参ったな、こっちは事務室の電話だから、あとで借りなおすのにもまたマスターにお願いしなきゃ──
lines.english: Damn. This was the office phone, which meant borrowing it again later would require another appeal to the boss—

lines.japanese: ──と思ってたらようやく出てくれました。カンペキ寝起きの声ですが。
lines.english: —and just as I thought that, she finally picked up, sounding utterly, unmistakably fresh out of bed.

lines.japanese: 「だから。誰だって聞いてんだけど」
lines.english: “I said, who is this?”

lines.japanese: 聞かれてません。いま初めて聞かれました。
lines.english: She hadn't. This was the first time she'd asked.

lines.japanese: ああ、そっか……そういや米田さん、すさまじく寝起き悪いんだっけ……。
lines.english: Ah, right... Yoneda was spectacularly bad at waking up...

lines.japanese: 「ち、千歳です。千歳鷲介。分かります？」
lines.english: “Ch-Chitose. Shusuke Chitose. Ring any bells?”

lines.japanese: 「んもう、米は送ってくれなくっていいってゆったじゃん、余るだけなんだからさー」
lines.english: “I told you not to send any more rice. It just piles up.”

lines.japanese: 「あのう、田舎のお母さんじゃなくて千歳です。将来大物んなる予定の千歳」
lines.english: “I'm not your mother back home. It's Chitose—Chitose, destined for greatness.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、千歳かー。でー、なによ」
lines.english: “Oh, Chitose. Whaddaya want?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、きのうの……ほら、放置された細川玉木さんの原稿を読んでもらおう大作戦なんすけどね」
lines.english: “It's about yesterday... You know, our Grand Campaign to Make Somebody Read Tamaki Hosokawa's Abandoned Manuscript.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あー」
lines.english: “Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese: 「あれから俺もいろいろ考えたんすけど、なかなかいい案が出なくて」
lines.english: “I've been thinking it over ever since, but I can't come up with a good plan.”

lines.japanese: 「そーお？　じゃあ昼間は百パー留守だから、小包なら局留めで送っといて。大丈夫、分かってるって」
lines.english: “Oh, really? I'm never home in the daytime, so send any packages to the post office for pickup. Don't worry. I know.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、めちゃめちゃ分かってないですよ！　待って待って！　千歳です、千歳ー！」
lines.english: “No, you don't get it at all! Wait, wait! It's Chitose! Chitose!”

lines.japanese: 切られそうな気配がして、俺は声の限りに呼びとめました。
lines.english: Sensing she was about to hang up, I called after her at the top of my lungs.

lines.japanese: 「んん～？　なぁに、分かってるよ千歳君……」
lines.english: “Mmm? What? I know, Chitose...”

lines.japanese: ほ、ほんとか？
lines.english: D-did she?

lines.japanese: 「ああ、よかった。ええと、きのうの件なんですけどね」
lines.english: “Oh, good. Well, about yesterday...”

lines.japanese: 「寝てます？　いま飛んでましたね？」
lines.english: “Are you asleep? You blanked out just now, didn't you?”

lines.japanese: 「や、手帳開いてたの。そっち、いまメモ用紙ある？」
lines.english: “No, I was opening my planner. You got something to write on?”

lines.japanese: あ、ページを繰る音。どうやら本当にもう目は覚めてるみたいです。
lines.english: Ah, pages turning. Apparently she really was awake now.

lines.japanese: 「メモメモ……はい、あります」
lines.english: “Paper, paper... Yes. Ready.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは四つの英字から始まる暗号みたいな文字を読みあげました。パソコンやウェブに疎い俺でも、それがどこかのホームページアドレスだってことぐらいは分かりました。
lines.english: Yoneda read out a coded-looking string that began with four English letters. Even someone as ignorant of computers and the Web as I was could tell it was a website address.

lines.japanese: 「私はまだ確認してないんだけど、沢井冴子が個人的なブログやってるって噂が社内にあって」
lines.english: “I haven't confirmed it myself, but there's a rumor around the company that Saeko Sawai keeps a personal blog.”

lines.japanese: 「え、じゃあこれって」
lines.english: “Then this is...?”

lines.japanese: 「そのサイトのＵＲＬ……なんかの参考になればと思って……」
lines.english: “The site's address... I thought it might give you something useful...”

lines.japanese: 「おおっ、ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Oh! Thank you very much.”

lines.japanese: 「んー」
lines.english: “Mmm.”

lines.japanese: ありがたいけど、ずいぶん眠そうだな米田さん。
lines.english: I was grateful, but Yoneda sounded terribly sleepy.

lines.japanese: 「すいません、安眠中お邪魔しちゃって。ブログは見ときますんで……あとなんか他に、沢井さん情報ってあります？」
lines.english: “Sorry to interrupt your peaceful slumber. I'll look over the blog... Anything else you know about Sawai?”

lines.japanese: 「眼鏡」
lines.english: “Glasses.”

lines.japanese: 「眼鏡。はい。それは俺もきのう見てますから」
lines.english: “Glasses. Right. I saw those myself yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 「あと、なんだっけ香水。アレ、チンパンジー」
lines.english: “And what was that perfume called? You know. Chimps-Élysées.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そんなブランドは絶対ないでしょうけど、近い名前で探しておきます。ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “There definitely isn't a perfume called that, but I'll look for something with a similar name. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「あとねー、昨日は遅くまでいたけど、残業を絶っっっ対しない日があるんだって。月曜日と金曜日」
lines.english: “Oh, and listen. She stayed late yesterday, but apparently there are two days when she ab-so-lute-ly never works overtime. Monday and Friday.”

lines.japanese: 「月曜……と、金曜すね。はい、ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Monday... and Friday. Right. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 俺は頭を下げながら、米田さん情報をメモに残していきました。
lines.english: I kept bowing as I jotted down each piece of Yoneda intel.

lines.japanese: でも米田さん、忙しいって言ってたのに、聞き込みみたいなことして調べてくれたんだなあ。たしかに手伝ってくれるとは言ってたけど、正直テキトーだと思ってた。
lines.english: She had said she was busy, yet she'd still gone around asking questions and investigating for me. She had promised to help, but honestly, I'd expected her to half-ass it.

lines.japanese: ごめんなさい米田さん。アンタほんまエエひとやで。
lines.english: I'm sorry I doubted you, Yoneda. You're good people. You really are.

lines.japanese: 「あー、あとなんだっけホラ、中学んときＢ組にいた黒鳥ちゃん。あの子結婚したんだって？」
lines.english: “Oh, and what was it? Kurotori, from Class B in middle school. I heard she got married?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、アナタの中学時代の同級生は存じあげません」
lines.english: “I'm afraid I don't know anyone you went to middle school with.”

lines.japanese: 米田さん……エエひとだけど……。
lines.english: Yoneda... was good people, but...

lines.japanese: まさかいまの情報、ぜんぶ夢の中で得たものじゃないですよねっ！？
lines.english: No. Surely every last scrap of that intel hadn't come to her in a dream!?

lines.japanese: 「あの、分かりました。もういいっす、もう寝てください。あっ、でもその前に、ひとつだけ確かめたいことがあるんです」
lines.english: “Okay, I get it. That's enough. Go back to sleep. Ah, but before you do, there's just one thing I need to confirm.”

lines.japanese: 「んー……？　なに」
lines.english: “Mmm...? What?”

lines.japanese: 「沢井さんって方、仕事はデキるんでしょうか」
lines.english: “Is Sawai good at her job?”

lines.japanese: しばらく無言が続きました。寝てるのかとも思いましたが、耳を澄ませば思案にふける唸り声が聞こえてきます。
lines.english: The silence lasted a while. I thought she might have fallen asleep, but when I listened closely, I heard a low, thoughtful hum.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、私とは仕事のやり方が違うけど、他部署から見たかぎり腕はいいと思うよ。付いてく作家さんもいるみたいだし。認めてさえもらえれば担当編集としては悪くないんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Well, her methods are different from mine, but looking in from another department, I think she's good. Some authors seem to stick with her, too. If you can win her over, she wouldn't be a bad editor to have.”

lines.japanese: 「そすか」
lines.english: “Got it.”

lines.japanese: それを聞いて安心しました。それなら応募作を見てもらうところまで漕ぎつければ、あとは完全に日和子さんの腕次第。
lines.english: That reassured me. If I could maneuver her into reading the manuscript, everything after that would rest entirely on Hiyoko's talent.

lines.japanese: そこで公正な評価が下されて駄目なら、まあそれは仕方がありません。
lines.english: And if a fair assessment found the manuscript wanting, then there was nothing to be done.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ米田さん、ありがとうございました」
lines.english: “All right. Thank you, Yoneda.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、あとは私、何も出来ないと思うけど、頑張ってね」
lines.english: “Mmm. I don't think there's anything else I can do, but good luck.”

lines.japanese: とんでもない。もう十分過ぎるほど助けていただきましたよ、米田さん。
lines.english: Hardly. She had already done more than enough for me.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、おやすみー……お父さんにもよろしくね……」
lines.english: “Well, good night... Say hello to your father for me...”

lines.japanese: どこまで目が覚めていたのか不安になる終わり方でしたが、ともかくケータイを切る音が聞こえて、米田さんとの会話は途切れました。
lines.english: That ending left me wondering how awake she had ever been. In any case, I heard the click of her hanging up, and our conversation was over.
“Now then...”

lines.japanese: 俺は受話器を所定の位置へ戻すと、今度はパソコンのディスプレイに向かいました。
lines.english: I returned the receiver to its cradle and turned toward the computer monitor.

lines.japanese: 偶然にもさっきマスターが、パソコンも使っていいとおっしゃっていました。ここはお言葉に甘えさせていただきましょう。
lines.english: By fortunate coincidence, the boss had just told me I could use the computer too. I would take him at his word.

lines.japanese: 俺は慣れない手つきでアドレスを打ちこんでいきました。
lines.english: With unpracticed hands, I typed in the address.

lines.japanese: ピンクを基調に、ファンシーな色や形が見栄えよく配置された画面。
lines.english: The screen was a confection of pink, with whimsical colors and shapes arranged to eye-catching effect.

lines.japanese: さすがは職業編集、こういう方面に造詣のある方なのでしょうか。なかなか手が込んでます。
lines.english: Maybe professional editors knew a thing or two about design. At any rate, the page was remarkably elaborate.

lines.japanese: プロフィール欄を見れば「さ　わ　こ　だ　よ　☆」と自己紹介。ハンドルネームってやつですか。あらま、可愛らしいお名前ですねい。
lines.english: The profile read, “i'm sa-wa-ko ☆.” That must be what they called a handle. My, what an adorable name.

lines.japanese: その右側には、上目遣いでこちらを見つめる裸眼の沢井さん。きのう祥玄社でお見かけしたより五つぐらい若返った、ポップ＆キュートな表情です。
lines.english: To its right was Sawai without her glasses, gazing up at the camera through her lashes. Her bright, adorable expression made her look five years younger than she had at Shogensha yesterday.

lines.japanese: おやおや？　他のどの写真を見ても、お顔の角度が図ったように同じですね？　ふしぎ！　なあんて野暮なツッコミは女性相手に失礼でしょうか。
lines.english: Oh? Her face was at precisely the same carefully measured angle in every photograph. How mysterious! But perhaps it would be ungentlemanly to point that out.

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、そんなことより精神統一だ」
lines.english: “No, no. Never mind that. Focus.”

lines.japanese: 仕事前にブラックコーヒーをがぶ飲みしてる余裕はありません。俺は鞄からカフェイン錠剤を取りだして飲みくだしました。たまの集中力増強アイテムとしては、これがなかなか馬鹿にならないんですよ。
lines.english: There was no time to sit around guzzling black coffee before my shift. I pulled a caffeine tablet from my bag and swallowed it. As an occasional concentration booster, the stuff was nothing to scoff at.

lines.japanese: さあ、パソコンを持たない俺としては、なんとかこの場で沢井編集の人となりを頭に収めたいところです。
lines.english: Since I didn't own a computer, I needed to commit everything I could about what made Sawai tick to memory here and now.

lines.japanese: それでは、このチカチカ目によろしくない画面と闘いましょう。
lines.english: All right, then. Time to do battle with this flickering assault on the eyes.

lines.japanese: こんなことで彼女の助けになり得るかは分かりませんが──
lines.english: I had no idea whether any of this could help her—

lines.japanese: ──とりあえず集中するんで、ちょいと失礼いたします。
lines.english: —but I needed to concentrate now, so if you'll excuse me for a moment.

lines.japanese: （見える）
lines.english: “(I can see it.)”

lines.japanese: （得られる）
lines.english: “(I can have it.)”

lines.japanese: （手が届く）
lines.english: “(It's within reach.)”

lines.japanese: （打ちつける）
lines.english: “(Pound against it.)”

lines.japanese: （擦りつける）
lines.english: “(Grind against it.)”

lines.japanese: （浴びせかける）
lines.english: “(Shower it all over.)”

lines.japanese: （鐘のアトモスフィア）
lines.english: “(An atmosphere of bells.)”

lines.japanese: （星のページェント）
lines.english: “(A pageant of stars.)”

lines.japanese: （雲のプラネタリウム）
lines.english: “(A planetarium of clouds.)”

lines.japanese: （翼を広げて）
lines.english: “(Spread your wings.)”

lines.japanese: （飛びたてる）
lines.english: “(You can fly.)”

lines.japanese: （きっと明日は飛びたてる！）
lines.english: “(Tomorrow, I know you can fly!)”
